positioning_check: ASIC aggregate short 0.24% as of 2026-09-21 (prev 0.2487% on 09-14, change -0.0087pp, slight covering), lag 4 sessions. That reading predates the 24 and 25 Sept drop (-5.0% then -17.1% on 13.7m shares, about 3x the 20-day median volume), so it says nothing about who sold into the drop. At 0.24% there is no squeeze fuel and no crowded short to fade. The priced lean of +0.79 is almost all the run-up term (-12.5% over 20d, -16.0% over 5d), i.e. a mean-reversion prior. outside_window.finding: The 24 Sept 2026 HMW update moved the 4ktpa LCE stabilised-rate target from 'within 2026' (July quarterly) to 'first half of calendar year 2027', and the 5.2ktpa expansion from 'H1 2027' to 'second half of calendar year 2027'. The release is headlined 'on track' and a wire summary (stocktitan) reported 'no changes to prior guidance'. Revenue slips about two quarters on a single-asset developer holding A$35.5m of cash at 30 June. The stock has already reacted -5.0% (24 Sept, with lithium peers PLS -5.7% and LTR -7.1%) and -17.1% (25 Sept, with peers only -2.5% to -3.6%). So the slip looks priced, and it is not re-resolved by the annual report inside the window. The next place it is tested is the September-quarter 5B, due by 31 Oct 2026 (cash burn, funding runway, whether a raise follows).

searched_and_found_nothing: ASX archive 2026, 12 months read: no trading halt, placement, Appendix 3B/2A issue of size, substantial-holder notice or results-date notice since the 24/09 update. The 11/09 Appendix 3H is a 500k performance-rights lapse dated 31/03/2025, immaterial.

Cause of the 25 Sept -17.1% move on 13.7m shares: no ASX announcement that day; trade-press searches (Stockhead, Small Caps, Listcorp 403) and web searches returned nothing. Lithium peers fell 2-4% that day, so about 13 points is idiosyncratic and unexplained. An unexplained drawdown is worth 0.

Going concern: the March 2026 half-year already carried a material-uncertainty paragraph from the directors and the reviewer (https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260313/pdf/06xdq9hbfk66f1.pdf). If the annual report repeats it, that is not news.

New auditor (Grant Thornton, 18 June 2026, https://announcements.asx.com.au/asxpdf/20260618/pdf/070s51s58mkfwz.pdf): the stated reason is the move to producer and a wider audit scope. There is no evidence of a dispute or a qualification. E&E of about A$198m at 31 Dec 2025 against a market cap of about A$400m (1.2675bn shares x A$0.315) makes an impairment on reclassification unlikely. Hypothesis only, sized 0.

Past annual-report reactions: 2023 +12.0% (in session; PLS +1.9%), 2024 0.0% next session, 2025 -10.0% next session with PLS -6.3% and LTR -10.7% the same day. So the annual report has carried sector beta and no idiosyncratic signal.

Appendix 5B section 8 (quarters of funding) could not be extracted from the July PDF: the tables did not decode, and the InvestingNews copy omits them. Burn is therefore unsourced beyond the A$35.5m closing cash.
No consensus and no broker previews were found. A search snippet quoted an A$0.80 average target (Stockopedia/marketbeat-style aggregator), which is not a print bar.
